reviews.text:
I had a really hard time finding a hospital I could entrust my beloved family member to, so I'm posting this in the hope that it will be helpful to others in a similar situation.

When my cat became ill and stopped eating her favorite food, I used to take her to a hospital near my home, but it was too far away, so I was advised to go to a nearby hospital where she would receive daily IV fluids.

Even after reading many hospital reviews, I couldn't find a hospital I could completely trust, so I consulted a friend.

My friend's acquaintance was taking her to this hospital and said it was very good, so I called and made an appointment.

As mentioned in the reviews, there can be a bit of a wait, but I personally think that's because the doctor is seriously and seriously committed to the life of each animal.

Also, it's always crowded, so I think it's inevitable that there will be a wait and that desired appointments will be fully booked, as it's a popular hospital.

My cat was in the very late stages of kidney failure, and the previous hospital told us she only had a few days left, which made us cry a lot. We had half resigned ourselves to the fact that she wouldn't make it, but we started going to this hospital anyway.

We went to the vet every day for IV fluids and injections, and consulted with the doctor whenever something came up. Given our cat's age, a complete recovery wasn't expected, but we tried various things, including starting a liquid diet.

After about two weeks of treatment, she became energetic enough to eat on her own.

For us, who had almost given up hope, this is almost a miracle. We are so grateful for our cat's efforts and for the caring and attentive care of the doctor and nurses.

I've seen reviews from people who are dissatisfied with the doctor or hospital, and I understand that disagreements between doctors and owners are inevitable in any hospital.

However, I hope that this helps as many pet owners as possible find a hospital where they can confidently entrust their family members.

There are doctors who treat patients without explaining the medication.

Based on this experience, I will not be using this hospital again. I hope this will be helpful to other pet owners who want to protect their precious family members.

The worst veterinary hospital experience I've ever had.

This will be long, but please read it.

My cat started drinking a lot of water, so I took her to the vet out of concern. She was diagnosed with diabetes.

The vet recommended Sembergo.

Why Sembergo instead of insulin?

Insulin requires two injections a day.

Sembergo is a bit more expensive, but it's an oral medication taken once a day.

This explanation... At this point, it's entirely from the owner's perspective.

Insulin and Sembergo are completely different medications with different uses. Without knowing this, and because I was afraid of injections, I chose Sembergo.

Two days later, she was vomiting, unable to drink water on her own, unable to stand, and exhibiting ketones, a state of ketoacidosis.

She couldn't eat, and her liver was strained, causing jaundice.

Later, I researched it and found out that

Sembergo is a recently released drug, with around 100 reported side effects in the last five months, and many cats have died. Unbelievable.

Of course, since it's a medication, it should be fine as long as you don't misuse it, but I used this medication without proper explanation and my cat almost died.
If they had properly diagnosed which medication was best for my cat, this wouldn't have happened.

They should have clearly explained the side effects of such a dangerous medication.

I called immediately after my cat developed ketones, but it was their day off. Telling me to bring her in immediately after the ketones appeared is irresponsible. Shouldn't they prescribe it, explain the side effects thoroughly, and provide end-of-life care?

I gave her this medication without realizing how dangerous it was, and took her to another vet. They saw her right away, cared for my panicked state, and thankfully, my cat and I are both healthy now.

I will never bring my cat to this vet again, and I strongly advise against it.

Even their explanation of food was inadequate.

The vet at my current vet said, "Choose something that tastes good!
Not eating is the worst thing!"

They explained that diabetic food isn't for removing sugar, but to slow down the rise in blood sugar after a rapid meal.

Don't worry about it so much.

The doctor here recommends Royal Canin.

Why? Did they just want to make money?

I've given it 1 star, but inwardly it's -100 stars.

I can't forgive them. I'll never forgive them again.
These days, they won't accept you without a reservation. I've tried calling to make a reservation for days, but I can't get through. How can they handle emergencies like this?

When I called to make an appointment for my first visit,
"We're fully booked for this morning's appointments,"
I was told.
So I asked, "What time is available this afternoon?"
I was then asked, "By the way, what are the symptoms?"
I explained that my pet had lost its appetite and was losing weight.
"I see. We're fully booked for the next week for first-time appointments,"
I was shocked.
Wait, weren't they only fully booked for the mornings?
Then why did they ask about the symptoms?
Did they think the symptoms were mild and therefore suggested a week later?
I thought, and said, "Never mind,"
and they replied, "I'm sorry."
I was furious, thinking they didn't mean it at all.
I was extremely upset that they downplayed my pet's symptoms based on this brief exchange, without even examining it directly.
I'm actually glad that my pet, who's like family to me, didn't have to be seen at a place like this.
I don't even want to give it one star.
I was truly disgusted in that single moment.
This is the clinic I always go to. They examine me very carefully and their explanations are easy to understand.
The doctor is very polite and responsible, but it's a little disappointing that I have to wait for over ten minutes every time, even though I have an appointment.

Our dog, Uru-kun, has been receiving care here since his second vaccination.

Today, he choked on his food, and we rushed him to this hospital in an emergency.

Even though it was past closing time and they were busy, they didn't give up and worked diligently until the very end, and even brought beautiful flowers. Thank you so much! 🙇‍♂️
Uru was all smiles! ☺️
During vaccinations and examinations, they give detailed explanations and thoughtful advice, suggesting what might be best. This is a very reassuring animal hospital.

You can really feel that the doctor and staff care for our pets very carefully.

We'll also bring our mischievous 6-year-old older sister here for her appointments!

If you're looking for a local veterinary hospital, I highly recommend this one!

Thank you so much for today! 🙇‍♂️

The previous hospital we went to completely disregarded our wishes, even deceiving us into performing tests we adamantly refused, and the tests were expensive, worsening our pet's condition.

That's why we switched to this hospital.

Because of the above experience, we had a thorough discussion with the doctor about the treatment plan from the very first visit.

We discussed things like, "This treatment will take this long and cost this much," and "I found this information online, and it seems to match my pet's symptoms."

The doctor then said, "This treatment is the safest option for now."

He explained that this treatment involves this process, costs this much, and the cause isn't entirely clear.

He mentioned that this medication isn't specifically for rodents, so it's a dog/cat medication with adjusted dosage, but there's no track record, and it's experimental.

The doctor also mentioned that he had seen a pet with similar symptoms to ours in the past, but didn't cure it using the method we were discussing.

He answered all our persistent questions. He's trustworthy.

Thanks to him, we're now receiving treatment without any doubts, and the results are positive.

The price was about what I expected.

It was half the price of my previous hospital.

What personally surprised me was that, even though the cause was known, they kept adding paid tests without my consent. Like a small test < medium test < large test.

Even though it was expected from the beginning that a large test would be necessary in the end.

Even so, it was cheaper than my previous hospital's follow-up visit, so although I still hold a grudge, I was able to forgive it to some extent.

When I pointed it out, I was told that they couldn't do anything if there was a limit on the cost.

Another issue was regarding how they handled the animals.

While the examination was fine, the nurse kept holding my unwilling pet the entire time I was listening to the doctor's explanation after the examination. She should have put it back in the carrier.

They seemed to think that every dog ​​and cat was tame and easy to handle.

I think the basic principle should be to minimize contact and be efficient, but there was absolutely no consideration for that.

My dog, who doesn't like excessive contact or being held even by his owner, was acting strangely after we got home, crying and complaining.

After comforting and caring for him, he calmed down in half a day.

At the previous vet we went to, he was so traumatized that even his owner was scared, and it took two months to heal him, so in that respect, this place is probably better.

I also referred to the reviews here before going, so I understand what you're saying very well. I think some people might find it unbearable.

The restraint technique was so good that I felt I could do it the same way even as an amateur, so I willingly do it myself.

They have a "do as you like" attitude, so I'm fine with that.

If they had been a little more considerate in this area, it would have been a perfect 5 stars.

Just to be clear, it's just the examination procedure and restraint that are disappointing; it doesn't mean they're treating the animals roughly.

The doctors and nurses are very kind.

I felt very relieved because even for minor concerns, they didn't give me the usual answers about the effects of food, but rather explained things from a medical perspective.

I've changed veterinary hospitals about three times since coming to Osaka.

I had my pet spayed at a veterinarian I know, which was far away. I was worried because I didn't have a reliable veterinary hospital to turn to in emergencies.

This hospital has clear pricing and the service is courteous.

Unfortunately, there are many hospitals that can't even provide the kind of service that I think is normal, but today was the first hospital in Osaka that I felt was truly good.

Thank you very much.

I haven't been able to go recently because I moved, but if I had a car, I would definitely want to go back to this hospital.

Animals can't speak, so sometimes it's hard to know what's wrong even if they're feeling unwell without a thorough examination.

However, if a pet owner is willing to do everything they can for their beloved pet, even if it costs money, the doctor will respond accordingly. ☺️

I was also very grateful for their care of my cat, Senju. She unfortunately passed away due to illness, but I'm still so thankful for everything they did until the very end. 💐
The nurses and doctors were very kind, and the price was reasonable. Even though I can't speak Japanese, they were willing to communicate with me via Google Translate. Thank you very much.

This is my first time owning a cat, so I didn't know what kind of treatment I needed, but they kindly explained everything over the phone, and I felt at ease because they were gentle with both my cat and me during the treatment. The doctor and nurses were so kind, I'm truly grateful! I was also glad they were able to accommodate me immediately even though I showed up without an appointment.

I'll definitely ask for their help again if anything comes up.

My two elderly dogs were cared for here for over a year while I was in Osaka.
They always treated me with great care during examinations and care, which was a great help.
The doctor really cares about animals, and the receptionists and nurses are also kind and polite, so I was able to leave my dogs in their care with peace of mind.
I would definitely recommend this animal hospital to anyone living in the neighborhood who has pets.

I received your care for about a year and a half until I moved.
When I first brought my kitten home, his diarrhea wouldn't go away, so I switched from another hospital to this one. They discovered that he was infected with giardiasis, and he made a full recovery.
At the time, I was troubled for about a month without knowing the cause, and I was getting exhausted, so I remember being relieved when you told me he would get better.
After that, when my cat caught a cat flu or conjunctivitis, you provided appropriate treatment, and thanks to you, my cat is still doing well today.

It was a great hospital, so I'm sad that I can no longer go there due to the move.
Thank you so much.

My cat had lost her appetite and was getting thin, so I took her to the vet, but all they did was give her an antibiotic injection.

I went back several times for advice, but she didn't get better with just injections, so I took her to another hospital, where they found fluid in her lungs, and she passed away shortly after.

I should have gone to another hospital sooner.

I don't understand why the reviews are so good.

The doctor didn't know how to treat me or what my illness was, and even though I only had a cold and rhinitis, he said I needed X-rays and other tests. When I refused, he said, "You don't understand Japanese," and had a very rude attitude during the treatment. When I asked if I even needed an X-ray, the doctor assumed I was a foreigner and didn't understand Japanese, and refused to interact with me at all. I repeatedly told him I had a viral illness, but he said he would only give me an antibiotic injection and couldn't provide any other medicine. Doesn't this discriminate against me from other Japanese people? Apparently, he hasn't even cured my cat.
Thank you for always taking care of me! The doctor is very kind and speaks frankly! I'm so glad I chose this hospital! They give me lots of helpful advice!

This is the worst hospital.
At first I thought it might be okay, but I was terribly mistaken. When the vet was tired, he gave the animal an injection very roughly, treated it roughly, and …

I have a hamster, and I often have to take him in for an emergency, but I've never been turned away. They always examine him thoroughly, and I can go home feeling relieved. Thank you so much as always!

The reason there are so many positive reviews is because the doctor is truly great! 😤
As someone with anxiety, I always appreciate how politely and gently he answers …
